 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Yogesh Khanna
 Order

Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.379/2017 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Bhajanpura, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 11.05.2014 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
One boy namely Bhavya aged seven years was born from this wedlock, who is in care and custody of respondent No.2.
However, due to matrimonial discord, the aforesaid FIR was registered on the complaint of respondent No.2 against the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 also filed a case under DV Act against the petitioner No.1.
During the pendency of proceedings, the couple settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 09.04.2021 arrived at before the Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.
The parties have also obtained divorce by mutual consent on 06.09.2021.
Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner No.1 agreed to pay Rs.4.22 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future, stridhan, and dowry articles etc.

Out of said sum, the petitioner No.1 has already paid Rs.3.00 Lacs to respondent No.2 and for the balance amount, the petitioner No.1 has handed over Fixed Deposit Receipt No.2811222446 dated 28.11.2022 drawn on Bank of Baroda for Rs.1.22 Lacs in favour of minor child of respondent No.2, which has been accepted by her.

3. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners having left with no claim against them and she has no Manoj And Ors vs The State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105536353/
1 objection if the FIR is quashed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

4. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
5. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.379/2017 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Bhajanpura and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
This order shall not affect any of the rights of the minor child which he may exercise, in future.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
